EDS elemental mapping of the 10Ti alloy is shown in Fig. 2, giving a typical example of the dendritic microstructure seen in these Nb-based refractory alloys, with enrichment of Nb and W having high melting points in the dendritic region, while enrichment of Hf and Ti with relatively lower melting points in the inter-dendritic region.
The XRD results shown in Fig. 3 confirm the single-phase bcc crystal structure in all the Nb-based refractory alloys that were studied here.
The main oxide is Nb2O5 in all alloys, which is kinetically favored in Nb-based alloys and known to be with non-protective nature.
An orthorhombic Hf6Nb2O17 forms at 1200 °C, which itself can be synthesized by solid-state reactions (e.g., annealing at high temperature) between HfO2 and Nb2O5 (6HfO2· Nb2O5).
Regarding Ti containing oxides or complex oxides, monoclinic Ti2Nb10O29 forms as the main Ti oxide, which itself can be synthesized by solid-state reactions between TiO2 and Nb2O5 (2TiO2⋅5Nb2O5).
WO3 forms in all W containing specimens.
